subject: Recoupment ladder and temporary uptime waiver - CloudScale
messages:
From: Alice Ng <alice@cloudscale.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary uptime waiver + recoupment ladder during migration

Hi Tessa / Laura,

Quick context — we are planning a staged migration of our public inference traffic into a private VPC deployment the weekend of Sep 11–13. The migration team expects a short period of degraded availability while the cross-region failover and model weights sync complete.

Because this is a customer-driven migration (compliance + data residency), we need to request a temporary SLA variance so we don't trigger standard recoupment bands for the two months following the cutover. Specifically: 1) a waiver that tolerates a measured uptime floor of 98.0% (instead of 99.5%) for Sep and Oct; 2) a recoupment ladder adjustment so monthly remedy credits are capped at a fixed dollar amount rather than token-proportional credits during that window.

We know this is non-standard — happy to work through the exact wording. Attached is our migration timeline + risk plan.

Can you let us know what your legal/ops would need to approve this and whether we can get a temporary amendment quickly? Our SRE lead (cc'd in a follow-up) will provide the measurement hooks for verifying failover windows.

Appreciate it,
Alice

Attachment: CloudScale-migration-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Ng <alice@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime waiver + recoupment ladder during migration

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We can accommodate a temporary amendment but we need to be explicit about the observation windows and the remedy cap so it doesn't create open-ended exposure.

High-level proposal from my side (draft attached):
- Temporary uptime floor: 98.0% for measurement months Sep 2026 and Oct 2026 only.
- Remedy structure: instead of per-token credits, apply a flat monthly cap of $50k for any month where uptime < 98.0%. Credits will be pro-rated if the measurement window is partial.
- Outage definition: measuring at the public API ingress (region us-west-2) per the same monitoring hooks we use in the hosted SLA; planned maintenance windows declared in advance will be excluded up to 4 hours per month.
- Start/end: amendment to take effect at 00:00 UTC Sep 11, 2026 and automatically revert to baseline on Nov 1, 2026, unless both parties agree to extend in writing.

We attached a redline-friendly PDF of the proposed amendment (proposed-sla-amendment-draft.pdf). Ben / Marcus — can you flag anything operational/legal that would block this? Laura — happy to route this through Contracts if we get alignment on the dollar cap and measurement clause.

Next step: Alice — if the above looks directionally OK, can you confirm the migration start date and the SRE contact who will triage any measurement disagreements? If you want us to prepare a DocuSign amendment, we can do that after a quick redline pass.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary uptime waiver + recoupment ladder during migration

Looping in a couple of operational points — quoting Alice's original note for context:

> Because this is a customer-driven migration (compliance + data residency), we need to request a temporary SLA variance so we don't trigger standard recoupment bands for the two months following the cutover.

Operational comments / asks:
1) Canary window: we need to confirm whether CloudScale will accept a canary window (24–72h) where traffic is progressively shifted. Our monitoring should define "failover incidents" as contiguous 5+ minute API error spikes that are customer-impacting. We need agreement on the canary ramp schedule to avoid counting intentional failover tests as outages.
2) Measurement granularity: will CloudScale accept our monthly 1-minute-sampled uptime calculation (the same algorithm used in the hosted SLA)? If not, please provide the SRE's preferred measurement methodology.
3) Remedy cap: $50k flat seems reasonable as a temporary mitigation, but Finance will want a short memo documenting why flat-dollar is preferable to token-based credits for this migration window.

If CloudScale can confirm the canary ramp and measurement acceptance, I'll prepare the internal memo and route the amendment to Contracts.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Reliability & Contracts, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — that all sounds workable. Quick answers:
- Canary ramp: we plan a progressive 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% shift over 48 hours, with rollback triggers at each step. We will treat any planned cutover activity declared in advance as excluded from outage counting (we'll publish the schedule 72 hours prior).
- Measurement: our SREs are fine with the 1-minute sample approach you mentioned. SRE contact is Miguel Rojas (miguel.rojas@cloudscale.com).
- Finance note: I'll add a short paragraph to our side explaining why we prefer a capped remediation (predictability for the migration budget).

Please proceed with the DocuSign path when you're ready. We'll aim to sign quickly.

Alice
VP, Platform — CloudScale
